findings.source_passage: he was as particular about the comfortable arrangement of his part of the boat, as an old stage-driver is about the snugness of his box
findings.why_it_matters: This simile is a distinctive voice-establishing comparison that characterizes Stubb's casualness with striking specificity; its omission flattens the portrait.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the stage-driver simile between 'invited guests' and the tinker-hammer comparison.

findings.source_passage: Tashtego now hunted in the wake of the great whales of the sea; the unerring harpoon of the son fitly replacing the infallible arrow of the sires
findings.source_locator: Tashtego paragraph, after description of aboriginal forests
findings.why_it_matters: The full rhetorical parallel—forest/sea, bow/harpoon, sires/son—is a recognizable signature construction; the draft reduces it to a truncated clause and loses the rhetorical balance and the woodland/moose backstory.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence with both halves of the parallel and the preceding woodland-hunting context.

findings.source_passage: you would almost have credited the superstitions of some of the earlier Puritans, and half-believed this wild Indian to be a son of the Prince of the Powers of the Air
findings.source_locator: Tashtego paragraph, final sentence before 'Tashtego was Stubb's squire'
findings.why_it_matters: This is an interpretively significant passage linking Tashtego to demonic/Puritan cosmology; it is critical-tradition material and entirely absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Puritan superstition / Prince of the Powers of the Air sentence in the Tashtego characterization.

findings.source_passage: Yet now, federated along one keel, what a set these Isolatoes were! An Anacharsis Clootz deputation from all the isles of the sea
findings.why_it_matters: The exclamation 'what a set these Isolatoes were!' is the rhetorical pivot before the Clootz sentence; the draft drops it, weakening the ironic force of the passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Yet now, federated along one keel, what a set these Isolatoes were!' before the Anacharsis Clootz sentence.

findings.source_passage: Little Flask was one of the wrought ones; made to clinch tight and last long. They called him King-Post
findings.source_locator: Flask paragraph, after carpenter's nails simile
findings.why_it_matters: The carpenter's-nails/wrought-nails/cut-nails division of mankind is a characteristically Melvillean aside; the draft collapses it and loses the taxonomic wit.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'As a carpenter's nails are divided into wrought nails and cut nails; so mankind may be similarly divided' before the King-Post identification.

findings.source_passage: prelusive of the eternal time, when sent for, to the great quarter-deck on high, he was bid strike in with angels, and beat his tambourine in glory
findings.why_it_matters: The draft omits 'beat his tambourine in glory' and the fuller phrasing 'to the great quarter-deck on high, he was bid strike in with angels'—the celestial imagery is the rhetorical payoff of the Pip prolepsis.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'beat his tambourine in glory' and the fuller quarter-deck/angels phrasing for the Pip closing lines.

summary: Three medium-severity losses (the stage-driver simile, the Puritan/Prince of the Powers of the Air sentence for Tashtego, and the 'what a set these Isolatoes were' exclamation) plus further voice flattenings throughout warrant regeneration.
